claims.statement: dcode chooses ACP before stdin processing; otherwise finalized stdin and message arguments select headless or interactive execution. Interactive and headless sessions preflight MCP, start a temporary loopback runtime, wait for health and the `agent` graph, bind server-validated durable workspace context, stream turns, and perform cancellation-safe cleanup.

The local runtime lifespan patches compatible in-memory run scheduling to wake on insertion and prebuilds the cached runtime; workspace runtimes pin compatible tracing settings, while thread leases and ownership tokens fence stale checkpoint writers.

Server shutdown is ownership-aware and platform-specific: POSIX uses a bootstrap parent-death pipe and process-group termination, while terminal stop prevents a racing restart from recreating the server.

Headless mode applies its surface-specific argument rules after stdin normalization: max-turns, timeout, quiet, no-stream, and rubric options require a headless message; auto-classifier is rejected, while explicit auto-approve and yolo flags are warned about and ignored.

RemoteAgent requires a configured workspace, binds or verifies a per-thread descriptor through the workspace route before streaming, sends that descriptor as run context, and adds thread-ownership headers while removing the incompatible configurable owner value.

The workspace route canonicalizes the requested directory, rejects client claims of project workspace policy, durably binds the thread, builds or validates the selected runtime before replying, and returns conflicts as 409 responses.

Headless resume never falls back to a new thread: it checks existence and age, rejects incompatible or unavailable persisted directories, can adopt the saved agent and model, and reserves a resumed thread before server startup.

After selecting a valid headless thread, dcode runs `--startup-cmd` before MCP metadata preload, thread reservation, and local-server startup; the command restores the project LangSmith environment, is non-fatal on launch, timeout, or nonzero exit, and cancellation terminates it without reserving a resumed thread.
Remote cancellation is best-effort for active runs; recovery state writes that conflict cancel pending and running runs with bounded waits and retry once.

CLI startup resolves the summarization model once and computes retry configuration for the selected model provider before ACP or session dispatch; provider retry settings in `--model-params` are overridden because dcode owns the retry budget.

The local server lifespan starts a cached runtime build while the client polls for health, and on shutdown cancels that build, shuts down server extensions, and performs a bounded best-effort LangSmith trace flush.

Server subprocess environment construction fixes the active profile and prevents persistent or scoped overrides from replacing profile, inherited Python path, or LangSmith carrier values before the loopback server starts.

Headless shell authorization is derived from the resolved shell allow-list: no list disables shell and auto-approves other tools, a restrictive list interrupts shell-only calls, and `all` enables unrestricted auto-approval; permission-request hooks override these shortcuts.

Headless quiet mode sends console output to stderr while response text writes directly to stdout; streaming writes chunks as they arrive, whereas `--no-stream` buffers final response text, and completed non-quiet runs can print usage statistics.
The headless loop counts its initial stream as turn one, resumes only while within `--max-turns` or its internal safety default, and returns exit code 124 when the HITL turn budget is exhausted.
Headless project hooks require explicit invocation trust; persisted interactive hook trust does not enable project hooks for a non-interactive run.
Help-only and selected lightweight diagnostic CLI paths avoid settings bootstrap and heavy runtime imports, preserving a startup fast path outside session execution.

For a non-quiet, MCP-enabled headless run, dcode starts MCP metadata preload after any startup command and before server setup, lets it overlap the subsequent work, and treats preload errors as non-fatal; after server readiness it uses a successful result only to report loaded tool count.

Headless sessions establish a client hook session before prompt submission; server lifecycle middleware emits hook requests through LangGraph interrupts, and the client deduplicates snapshot-scoped fulfillment then merges hook and HITL responses into a resume command.

Headless dispatch reports OSC 7501 `working` before execution and maps its final exit in a finally block to a persistent done, error, or clear record; interactive status instead tracks working, blocked permission/question prompts, and the most recent outcome until the app closes.
